title: Cover-Up
summary: A careful intruder got in with a reused password and left several ways back in - an extra key, a scheduled beacon, and a note - then tried to tidy up after themselves. Find all of it and shut every door.
story: You run db3, a database server for {{CO}} (made up), on 10.10.9.0/24. The security team saw a short connection from an unexpected address and handed it to you. You have a root console on db3. The attacker tried to clean up, but not everything is gone.
goal: Work out the account the intruder reused and the address they came from, find the three things they left (an extra SSH key, a scheduled beacon, and a dropped note with the flag), and remove every one - plus lock the account - before the beacon copies the database out.
skills: auth logs, bash history, authorized_keys, cron jobs, locking an account, thorough clean-up

flags.name: The flag in the dropped note

questions.ask: Which account did the intruder reuse to get in?
questions.explain: The successful sign-in in /var/log/secure is for this database account.

questions.ask: What address did they connect from?
questions.explain: The same address is on the sign-in and in the account's bash history (an scp back to it).

questions.ask: What is the comment on the extra SSH key they added to the account?
questions.explain: The last line of ~/.ssh/authorized_keys is a key you did not add; its comment is the attacker's handle.

tasks.name: Remove the attacker's extra SSH key

attacker.note: The scheduled beacon fired and staged a database dump in /tmp/.x, ready to send out.

hints.text: The sign-in log and the account's own shell history tell you who and from where; history -c doesn't empty the file on disk.
Three ways back in: a key, a schedule, a dropped note. Remove the first two and lock the account.
